To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a mix of fermentable fibers limits overfeeding-induced metabolic alterations in minipigs, with a beneficial effect on body weight gain, hepatic lipids accumulation and glucose handling by the liver.

the addition of a mix of fermentable fibers (inulin + pectin + resistant starch) in the diet of overfed minis prevented the increase in liver lipids content and body weight gain induced by overfeeding, but did not improve insulin sensitivity or glucose tolerance.
a supplementation of a specific mix of fibers can limit body weight gain and the accumulation of lipid droplets in the liver induced by overfeeding in minipigs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of a mix of dietary fibers in a minipig model of overfeeding.
the effect of a mix of dietary fermentative fibers in a model of overfeeding.
the impact of a mix of dietary fibers on metabolic perturbations induced by a diet rich in lipids and sugars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a supplementation of a mixture of fermentable fibers can limit the accumulation of lipids droplets in the liver of overfeeding pigs and improve the handling of lipids and glucose by this organ, but with a complex and not fully explained regulation.
fibers supplementation in the diet of minipigs overfed for 56 days limits body weight gain and liver fat accumulation.
the supplementation with fibers improved hepatic lipids handling in overfed minipig, but not glucose metabolism, which was only improved on a short-term basis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a mix of dietary fibers improves lipids and glucose metabolism of the liver of over-fed minipigs, but the underlying mechanisms remain to be determined.
the supplementation of dietary fermentable fiber mix in overfed minipig model can limit body weight gain and hepatic steatosis, with no effect on insulin resistance.
a mix of dietary fibers can improve hepatic metabolism in overfed minipig, by limiting the accumulation of hepatics lipids and by improving glucose metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the supplementation of fibers can limit the accumulation of lipids in the liver induced by overfeeding in minipigs.
a supplementation of dietary fibers could improve the metabolic perturbations induced by overfeeding in minipigs, with a potential role on hepatic steatosis.
a mix of fermentable fibers is able to limit overfeeding-induced metabolic disturbances and to improve hepatic metabolism in minipigs.
